name: Copernican Suite – DriftGuard Integration and Policy v2
goals: Introduce DriftGuard as an internal, modular policy engine in the Copernican Suite repository.
Migrate existing ad-hoc metadata/policy scripts to DriftGuard rules.
Clean up and stabilise the repository policy (Last Updated, version sync, changelog discipline, etc.).
Reduce CI/pre-commit failures due to policy oversights by providing a single dev-suite entrypoint.
Prepare DriftGuard to be spun off into a standalone project with a stable API and spec.

lint_tools_to_keep.purpose: Code formatter. Enforces consistent Python formatting with line length 79.
Import sorter. Keeps imports ordered and grouped consistently (Black profile, line length 79).
Fast Python linter and simple static analysis. Replaces most uses of flake8/pyflakes/pycodestyle while also auto-fixing some issues.
Additional linter. Currently kept to catch any checks not yet covered/configured in Ruff. Can be reconsidered later once Ruff fully subsumes it.
Ensures text files end with a single newline. Helps avoid noisy diffs across platforms.
Removes trailing whitespace from lines. Keeps diffs clean.

driftguard_module.description: Internal implementation of DriftGuard as a Python package living inside the Copernican repo, but written to be spin-off ready.
design_constraints: Code under driftguard/ must not import copernican_lib, engines or any Copernican-specific modules.
DriftGuard must operate only on the filesystem (paths, globs) and the project policy spec (driftguard.yml).
The public API (Python and CLI) should be small and stable so it can later become a standalone package with minimal changes.

directories_and_files.purpose: Expose a simple helper like load_engine(repo_root=None) that loads the policy spec and returns a PolicyEngine instance.
Define data classes for the DriftGuardSpec (surfaces, rulesets, metrics) and a load_spec() function that reads driftguard.yml.
Define the PolicyEngine class with check() and fix() methods. Orchestrates rule execution and aggregates violations and metrics.
Expose get_all_rules(spec) and the Rule, RuleContext, Violation, Metric base types.
Implement metadata-related rules: LastUpdatedDocsRule, VersionSyncRule, NoFutureDatesRule, CitationYamlRule, ChangelogRule.
Implement Python library rules: NoPrintInLibRule, NewModulesNeedTestsRule, optional BugfixHasTestRule (soft warning).
Implement drift metrics: TodoCountRule, TestCouplingRule, DocAgeRule. These provide Metric values but usually no hard violations.
Utility helpers shared across rules: reading files, resolving globs from the spec, querying git status for new/changed files, date helpers.
CLI entrypoint implementing commands: `driftguard check`, `driftguard fix`, `driftguard metrics`. Uses the same PolicyEngine APIs.

load_engine.behavior: Resolve the repo root, load driftguard.yml via load_spec(), construct and return a PolicyEngine.

methods.name: check
methods.description: Run all configured rules on the given scope (staged files or full repo) and mode (fast/full). Returns violations plus drift metrics.

methods.name: fix
methods.signature: fix(scope: str = 'staged', safe_only: bool = True) -> list[str]
methods.description: Apply safe auto-fixes (e.g. Last Updated header insert/update, simple synonyms). Returns textual messages describing applied fixes.

commands.name: check
commands.behavior: Run PolicyEngine.check() and print violations. Exit non-zero if any hard violations are present; soft warnings do not fail the process.

commands.name: fix
commands.behavior: Run PolicyEngine.fix() and print messages. Should not introduce unsafe changes; typically used on staged files before commit.

commands.name: metrics
commands.behavior: Run PolicyEngine.check() in full mode and print drift metrics only, in human-readable or JSON form. Never fails the process.

tests.purpose: Unit tests for PolicyEngine: combining rules, aggregation of violations/metrics, handling of scope/mode, basic error handling.
Tests for LastUpdatedDocsRule, VersionSyncRule, NoFutureDatesRule, CitationYamlRule, ChangelogRule.
Tests for NoPrintInLibRule, NewModulesNeedTestsRule and any other Python-library-specific rules.
Tests for drift metric rules: TODO counting, test-coupling ratio estimation, document age calculations.

Meta-test: if driftguard.yml is modified in a commit, ensure at least one driftguard/*.py and one tests/test_driftguard_*.py file are also modified. This keeps the spec, implementation and tests in sync.

driftguard_yaml_spec.description: Initial DriftGuard policy specification for the Copernican Suite. This will live as YAML at the repository root (driftguard.yml). The JSON structure here is a direct representation of the intended YAML.

metrics.name: todo-count
metrics.description: Total count of TODO/FIXME/XXX markers found in core library and engine code.

metrics.name: test-coupling-ratio
metrics.description: Approximate fraction of core modules that appear to have corresponding tests. Below this threshold emits a warning.

metrics.name: doc-age-days
metrics.description: Maximum age in days of key docs (README, AGENTS, CONTRIBUTING, docs/*). If any exceeds this, emit a drift warning.

implementation_notes: DriftGuard should treat the spec as the single source of truth for which rules apply to which file patterns.
Rules are referenced by name (e.g. 'last-updated-header') and mapped to concrete Rule implementations in driftguard/rules/*.py.
The allow-list style approach (surfaces with include/exclude) avoids accidental overreach like enforcing Last Updated on code modules.
Surfaces can be extended in future without changing DriftGuard core; only the YAML and possibly new rules need to change.

repository_policy_summary.description: Summary of the agreed repository policy for the Copernican Suite, encoded both as structured data and as a markdown section to be added to README.md and AGENTS.md.

source_of_truth.canonical_spec: driftguard.yml at the repository root is the single source of truth for policy configuration.
source_of_truth.driftguard_role: DriftGuard reads the spec, applies rules to surfaces, computes violations and drift metrics, and exposes both a CLI and a Python API.
source_of_truth.human_summary: README.md and AGENTS.md each contain a 'Development Laws (DriftGuard Policy)' section that summarises the policy and points back at driftguard.yml.

last_updated_policy.remove_headers_from: All other files: library code, tests, tools, workflows, lockfiles, etc.
last_updated_policy.no_future_dates: Last Updated dates must never be in the future; DriftGuard enforces this where headers are required.

version_sync.enforcement: DriftGuard replaces tools/check_meta.py and tools/precommit_custom_checks.py for version consistency checks.

changelog.requirement: Any non-trivial change in behaviour, interface, or policy must have a corresponding entry in the latest section of CHANGELOG.md.
changelog.enforcement: DriftGuard's ChangelogRule checks for code/doc changes without a matching changelog update and flags them.

conflict_markers.policy: Old git conflict marker rules are removed from policy. Merge conflicts are handled at the Git level, not by DriftGuard.

code_and_tests.new_modules_need_tests: Any new Python module under copernican_lib/ or engines/ must be accompanied by new or updated tests under tests/. DriftGuard treats violations as hard errors.
code_and_tests.no_print_in_lib: Library and engine code must not use bare print(); use copernican_lib.console_output or the logger abstraction instead. Tests and tools may still use print().
code_and_tests.bugfix_practice: Bugfixes listed in the changelog should have corresponding tests that would fail without the fix; DriftGuard may emit warnings when bugfix entries lack test changes.

format_and_lint: Ruff for linting and simple static analysis.
Flake8 for additional linting coverage while transitioning fully to Ruff.
pre-commit-hooks: end-of-file-fixer and trailing-whitespace for hygiene.
tooling_and_workflows.driftguard_role: DriftGuard complements these tools by enforcing repository-specific policy (metadata, tests, versioning, drift metrics).
tooling_and_workflows.dev_suite: tools/dev_suite.py will provide a one-command local check: format, lint, DriftGuard fix+check, then run tests. This should be run before committing.

ci_and_drift.ci_checks: CI must run driftguard check --scope=repo --mode=full. Hard violations fail the build; drift metrics are logged but only cause failures if thresholds are explicitly configured to do so.
metrics: todo-count: number of TODO/FIXME/XXX markers in core code.
test-coupling-ratio: fraction of core modules that appear to have matching tests.
doc-age-days: maximum age of key docs since their Last Updated date.
ci_and_drift.positive_drift_goal: Over time, the policy should encourage adding tests, keeping docs fresh, reducing TODO debt, and tightening the rules where it makes sense.

repository_policy_summary.development_laws_markdown_block:
## Development Laws (DriftGuard Policy)

This repository uses **DriftGuard** as a live policy layer for human+AI development.

- The **canonical machine-readable policy** is defined in `driftguard.yml`.  
  This file describes:
  - which files belong to which surfaces (docs, interfaces, library code, etc.),
  - which rules apply to each surface,
  - which drift metrics are tracked, and with what thresholds.

- This section is a human-readable summary. In case of mismatch, `driftguard.yml` is the source of truth.

### Docs and metadata

- Only the following files must carry a `Last Updated:` header:
  - `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  - all `docs/**/*.md`
  - `CITATION.cff`, `LICENSE.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`
  - `copernican.py`
  - `start.sh`, `start.command`, `start.bat`
  - `copernican_lib/config_schemas/**/*.yml`
  - `models/**/*.yml`
- All other files (library code, tests, tools, workflows, lockfiles, etc.) must **not** have a `Last Updated` header.
- `Last Updated` dates must never be in the future. DriftGuard enforces this for the files that require headers.
- A single semantic version `X.Y.Z` must be consistent across:
  - `copernican_lib/VERSION`
  - `README.md` (where it appears)
  - `CITATION.cff`
  - packaging metadata.
- Any non-trivial change in behaviour, interface, or policy must add an entry to the latest section of `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Conflict-marker rules are not enforced by policy; Git/merge tools handle them.

### Code and tests

- New Python modules under `copernican_lib/` and `engines/` must be accompanied by new or updated tests under `tests/`.  
  DriftGuard treats “new module with no test changes” as a hard violation.
- Library and engine code (`copernican_lib/**/*.py`, `engines/**/*.py`) must not use bare `print()`.  
  Use the logging / console abstraction instead.
- Tests and tooling scripts may use `print()` where appropriate.
- Bugfixes:
  - Any bugfix noted in `CHANGELOG.md` should be backed by a test that would fail without the fix.
  - DriftGuard currently treats “bugfix with no test change” as a warning, not a hard error.

### Tools and workflows

- The codebase is formatted and linted with:
  - **Black** (formatting),
  - **isort** (import ordering),
  - **Ruff** (linting and simple quality checks),
  - **Flake8** (additional linting),
  - **pre-commit-hooks** (`end-of-file-fixer`, `trailing-whitespace`) for basic hygiene.
- **DriftGuard** does not replace these tools; it complements them by enforcing project-specific policy and drift limits.
- A local dev script (e.g. `python tools/dev_suite.py`) should be run before committing. It:
  - runs formatting and linting,
  - runs DriftGuard in fast mode on staged files (and may apply safe autofixes),
  - runs a relevant subset of tests.

### CI and drift

- CI runs `driftguard check` in full mode on the whole repository:
  - Hard violations (broken policy) fail the build.
  - Drift metrics (e.g. TODO count, test–module coupling, document age) are computed and logged.
- Drift metrics have thresholds configured in `driftguard.yml`. Crossing a threshold emits a warning and may eventually be promoted to a hard error.
- The goal is **positive drift**:
  - adding tests when new modules appear,
  - keeping documentation and metadata fresh,
  - gradually reducing TODO/FIXME debt,
  - tightening policy over time rather than loosening it.

create.description: New package root for DriftGuard. Expose load_engine() and version metadata if needed.
Implements DriftGuardSpec data structures and load_spec() that reads driftguard.yml.
Implements PolicyEngine with check() and fix() methods, orchestrating all rules.
Defines base classes for Rule, RuleContext, Violation, Metric and a get_all_rules() factory.
Metadata and documentation rules: LastUpdatedDocsRule, VersionSyncRule, NoFutureDatesRule, CitationYamlRule, ChangelogRule.
Python-library rules: NoPrintInLibRule, NewModulesNeedTestsRule, BugfixHasTestRule (warning-only to start).
Drift metric rules: TODO counting, test-coupling ratio estimation, doc-age in days.
Helper functions used by rules and PolicyEngine (file loading, globbing, git inspection, date helpers).
CLI for DriftGuard with commands: check, fix, metrics.
Project-local DriftGuard policy spec, matching the structure in plan.driftguard_yaml_spec.spec_object.
Convenience script that runs formatting, linting, DriftGuard fix+check, and tests in a single command.
Unit tests for PolicyEngine and core orchestration.
Unit tests for drift metric rules.
Meta-test ensuring that edits to driftguard.yml are accompanied by edits to driftguard/*.py and tests/test_driftguard_*.py.

modify.description: Replace the local 'copernican-policy' hook (tools/precommit_custom_checks.py) with a DriftGuard hook that runs `driftguard check --scope=staged --mode=fast`. Optionally add a manual `driftguard fix` hook. Also remove the Last Updated header from this file as it is not a policy surface.
Ensure CI runs `driftguard check --scope=repo --mode=full` and optionally `driftguard metrics --format=json`. Keep pytest tests and build steps as-is.
No major logic change; it will still run pre-commit on all files, which now includes DriftGuard. Remove or update any mention of legacy policy scripts if present.
Delete this workflow entirely (see file_operations.delete). CI already runs tests; the dedicated tests.yml is redundant.

Add or replace the 'Development Laws' section with the new 'Development Laws (DriftGuard Policy)' markdown block provided in plan.repository_policy_summary.development_laws_markdown_block. Ensure this section clearly points to driftguard.yml as canonical. Keep Last Updated header, since README is a doc surface.

Add the same 'Development Laws (DriftGuard Policy)' section as in README.md. It should contain identical content so humans and AIs read the same laws. Keep Last Updated header (AGENTS.md is a doc surface).
Update any existing policy text to reference DriftGuard and driftguard.yml instead of legacy scripts. Optionally link to the Development Laws section in README/AGENTS. Keep Last Updated header.
Fix the YAML structure and author metadata as previously agreed (Apostol Apostolov & Black Epsilon Ltd., Bulgaria). Ensure Last Updated and date-released fields are correct and not in the future.

Keep this script as-is or adjust only if necessary to cooperate with DriftGuard (e.g. no longer responsible for Last Updated changes; DriftGuard covers metadata policy). Ensure tests/test_update_lock.py still pass.
Either delete or rewrite this test to validate DriftGuard behaviour instead of tools/precommit_custom_checks.py. The end state should have no test importing tools/precommit_custom_checks.py.
Either delete or rewrite this test to validate DriftGuard's metadata rules (LastUpdatedDocsRule, VersionSyncRule, NoFutureDatesRule) instead of tools/check_meta.py.

Remove any existing Last Updated headers from Python modules, tests, tools and CI configs that are not in the allow-listed surfaces. This may be done by DriftGuard autofix, or with a one-time clean-up pass.

delete.description: Legacy ad-hoc pre-commit policy script, superseded by DriftGuard. Remove after its logic is migrated into DriftGuard rules.
Legacy metadata checker script, superseded by DriftGuard metadata rules. Remove after tests are migrated to the new rules.
Legacy tests-only workflow. CI already runs tests in ci.yml, so this workflow is redundant and can be removed.

phases.name: Phase 0 – Preparation and alignment
steps: Ensure the current Copernican Suite repository is clean (no uncommitted changes).
Open and review .pre-commit-config.yaml, tools/precommit_custom_checks.py, tools/check_meta.py, tests/test_precommit_custom_checks.py and tests/test_check_meta.py to understand existing policy logic.
Review README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff and docs/ to see where current development laws and metadata expectations are documented.
Decide on the final path and name for the DriftGuard policy spec file (driftguard.yml at repository root).

phases.name: Phase 1 – Introduce DriftGuard skeleton
steps: Create the driftguard/ package directory with __init__.py, spec.py, core.py, rules/__init__.py, rules/metadata.py, rules/python_lib.py, rules/drift.py and utils.py as empty or minimally stubbed modules.
In driftguard/spec.py, define data classes for DriftGuardSpec, SurfaceConfig, DriftMetricConfig and a load_spec() function that reads driftguard.yml (temporary placeholder content at first).
In driftguard/core.py, define the PolicyEngine class with stubbed check() and fix() methods returning empty violations/metrics.
In driftguard/rules/__init__.py, define the Rule, RuleContext, Violation and Metric base types and a get_all_rules(spec) function that initially returns an empty list.
Add driftguard/cli.py with a basic main() that parses 'check', 'fix' and 'metrics' commands but only prints placeholder messages for now.
Wire up the console script entry point in pyproject.toml (or equivalent): `driftguard = driftguard.cli:main`.
Add initial tests (tests/test_driftguard_core.py) that at least import PolicyEngine and verify that check() and fix() run without crashing with an empty spec.

phases.name: Phase 2 – Create driftguard.yml and port policy surfaces
steps: Create driftguard.yml at the repository root, following the structure in plan.driftguard_yaml_spec.spec_object.
Implement load_spec() in driftguard/spec.py to parse this YAML into DriftGuardSpec objects (handle errors clearly; fail fast with a useful message if the spec is invalid).
Extend driftguard/rules/__init__.py.get_all_rules(spec) to instantiate rule objects for each rule name referenced in the spec (e.g. 'last-updated-header', 'version-sync', 'no-print').
Implement RuleContext so that rules can discover which files belong to which surfaces based on the include/exclude globs defined in the spec.
Add or update tests (test_driftguard_core.py) to validate that surfaces are resolved correctly from driftguard.yml and that get_all_rules() returns the expected rule instances.

phases.name: Phase 3 – Implement metadata rules (Last Updated, version sync, changelog, citation)
steps: In driftguard/rules/metadata.py, implement LastUpdatedDocsRule:
- Identify files on the 'docs' and 'interfaces' surfaces that require a Last Updated header.
- Check that required files have a header in one of the accepted forms.
- Verify that Last Updated dates are not in the future.
- Do not require Last Updated to match today's date; only require that it exists where needed and is not futuristic.
- Implement fix() to insert or update headers for missing/invalid cases, but only for files in the required surfaces.
Implement VersionSyncRule:
- Read the canonical version (e.g. from copernican_lib/VERSION).
- Verify that README.md, CITATION.cff and packaging metadata mention the same version.
- Report violations when inconsistencies are found.
Implement NoFutureDatesRule (if not already part of LastUpdatedDocsRule):
- Scan required surfaces for date patterns that are later than today.
- Report violations but do not auto-fix.
Implement CitationYamlRule:
- Parse CITATION.cff as YAML; confirm it is structurally valid and contains the required fields (cff-version, title, version, date-released, authors, preferred-citation).
- Optionally verify that version and date-released match the main version and Last Updated for CITATION.cff.
Implement ChangelogRule:
- Use git status or direct diffing to detect when non-trivial files have changed (code or docs).
- Check that the latest section of CHANGELOG.md has been modified in the same commit (or run) when such changes exist.
- Report violations if code/docs changed but no changelog entry was added.
Port logic from tools/check_meta.py and tools/precommit_custom_checks.py into these DriftGuard rules instead of re-implementing it from scratch.
Update tests/test_check_meta.py to call DriftGuard's metadata rules (or create new tests/test_driftguard_rules_metadata.py and retire test_check_meta.py).
Update or replace tests/test_precommit_custom_checks.py with tests that validate DriftGuard metadata rule behaviour instead of the legacy precommit_custom_checks module.

phases.name: Phase 4 – Implement Python library rules (no-print, new-modules-need-tests, bugfix coverage)
steps: In driftguard/rules/python_lib.py, implement NoPrintInLibRule:
- Apply to the 'python-lib' surface (copernican_lib/**/*.py, engines/**/*.py, excluding tests/tools/driftguard).
- Flag any occurrence of 'print(' that is not in tests/tools.
- Do not attempt auto-fixes; just report violations.
Implement NewModulesNeedTestsRule:
- Use git status or diff to detect newly added Python modules under the 'python-lib' surface.
- Verify that at least one file under tests/ changed in the same commit/run.
- Treat missing test updates for new modules as hard violations.
Implement BugfixHasTestRule as a warning rule:
- Parse the latest section of CHANGELOG.md.
- Detect entries that are clearly bugfix-related (e.g. contain 'Bugfix' or similar tags).
- Check whether files mentioned in those entries have corresponding test changes in tests/.
- Emit warnings if bugfix entries lack matching test updates.
Add tests in tests/test_driftguard_rules_python_lib.py to ensure these rules correctly detect and report conditions on synthetic file trees.

phases.name: Phase 5 – Implement drift metrics (TODOs, test coupling, doc age)
steps: In driftguard/rules/drift.py, implement TodoCountRule:
- Count occurrences of TODO/FIXME/XXX markers in core library and engine code.
- Return a Metric with name 'todo-count' and the computed value.
Implement TestCouplingRule:
- For each Python module in copernican_lib/ and engines/, try to infer a corresponding test file (e.g. tests/test_<module>.py or similar naming heuristics).
- Estimate the fraction of modules that appear to be covered by tests.
- Return a Metric 'test-coupling-ratio' with that value.
Implement DocAgeRule:
- For key docs (README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/**/*.md), read their Last Updated header and compute age in days relative to today.
- Return a Metric 'doc-age-days' equal to the maximum age observed.
Ensure that these rules normally do not create hard violations; they primarily produce metrics, with thresholds encoded in driftguard.yml.
Add tests in tests/test_driftguard_rules_drift.py that operate on synthetic directories to validate metric calculations and threshold behaviour.

phases.name: Phase 6 – Wire DriftGuard into pre-commit, CI and dev suite
steps: Modify .pre-commit-config.yaml to remove the 'copernican-policy' hook that calls tools/precommit_custom_checks.py.
Add a new local hook that calls `driftguard check --scope=staged --mode=fast` with language: system and pass_filenames: false.
Optionally add a manual pre-commit hook `driftguard-fix` that can be run explicitly to apply safe auto-fixes on staged files.
Modify .github/workflows/ci.yml to run `driftguard check --scope=repo --mode=full` after dependencies are installed and before or after tests.
Add a CI step that runs `driftguard metrics --format=json > driftguard_metrics.json` and uploads this file as an artifact if desired.
Leave lint.yml mostly unchanged, since it already runs pre-commit against all files; as soon as DriftGuard is in pre-commit, it will be exercised there.
Remove .github/workflows/tests.yml; CI already runs tests inside ci.yml, and the extra workflow is redundant.
Create tools/dev_suite.py that orchestrates Black, isort, Ruff, DriftGuard fix+check, and pytest, so that developers and Codex can run a single command before committing.

phases.name: Phase 7 – Policy clean-up: Last Updated headers and legacy scripts
steps: Use DriftGuard (or a one-off script) to remove Last Updated headers from all files that are not in the allow-listed surfaces (code modules, tests, tools, workflows, lockfiles, etc.).

Confirm that Last Updated headers remain only in README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/**/*.md, CITATION.cff, LICENSE.md, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, copernican.py, start.* scripts, config schema YAMLs and model YAMLs.
Verify that CITATION.cff has the corrected structure and author metadata (Apostol Apostolov & Black Epsilon Ltd., Bulgaria) and that DriftGuard's CitationYamlRule passes.
Once DriftGuard metadata rules fully cover the old checks, delete tools/precommit_custom_checks.py and tools/check_meta.py from the repository.

Retire or repurpose tests/test_precommit_custom_checks.py and tests/test_check_meta.py so that no tests import these legacy modules anymore, and all relevant behaviour is tested via DriftGuard-specific tests instead.

phases.name: Phase 8 – README/AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING alignment
steps: Insert the 'Development Laws (DriftGuard Policy)' markdown block (plan.repository_policy_summary.development_laws_markdown_block) into README.md at the appropriate section.
Insert the same block into AGENTS.md, ensuring the content is identical so both humans and AI agents read the same laws.
Update CONTRIBUTING.md to reference DriftGuard and driftguard.yml as the canonical policy instead of legacy scripts. Link to the Development Laws section in README/AGENTS for human-readable guidance.
Run DriftGuard check in full mode to ensure Last Updated headers, version sync and changelog requirements are all satisfied after these edits.

phases.name: Phase 9 – Validation, tuning and spin-off readiness
steps: Run the full test suite (pytest) and ensure all tests, including the new DriftGuard tests, pass.
Run driftguard check --scope=repo --mode=full locally and confirm zero hard violations and reasonable drift metrics.
Adjust driftguard.yml thresholds (todo-count, test-coupling-ratio, doc-age-days) if initial values are too strict or too lax, aiming for useful warnings without constant noise.

Document (in README/AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING) how future changes to policy should be made: edit driftguard.yml, update DriftGuard rules/tests and reflect changes in the human-readable Development Laws section.
Confirm that DriftGuard is fully self-contained under driftguard/ and that nothing in that package imports Copernican-specific modules.

At this point DriftGuard is ready to be split into a standalone repository: copy driftguard/ into a new project, add its own pyproject.toml and tests, and make Copernican depend on it via a normal dependency instead of the in-tree package.

general: Always treat driftguard.yml as the canonical policy spec. When in doubt, refer to it rather than hard-coding assumptions.
When editing multiple files that relate to policy, try to update driftguard.yml first, then adjust DriftGuard rules and tests to match.
Use the existing code style in copernican_lib and tests as a reference for DriftGuard's coding style (type hints, docstrings, imports).
implementation_order_hint: Follow the phases in plan.phases in order. Phases 1–3 are the minimum to get DriftGuard running with metadata rules; later phases refine behaviour and drift metrics.
Implement DriftGuard skeleton and spec loading before wiring it into pre-commit and CI. Avoid breaking existing workflows until the new system is in place.
Port logic from tools/precommit_custom_checks.py and tools/check_meta.py into DriftGuard rules incrementally, running tests frequently to avoid regressions.
Only delete the legacy scripts once all their responsibilities are clearly covered by DriftGuard rules and tests.
After DriftGuard is in place, prioritise getting tools/dev_suite.py working. This script is the key to reducing CI failures for both you and Codex.
token_budget: When working with Codex on implementing this plan, you do not need to paste the entire PLAN.json each time.
Instead, reference specific sections (phases, file_operations, driftguard_module) and work on a small, defined subset of steps per session.
Keep prompts focused on one phase or a few closely related steps to minimise token usage and reduce context noise.
